verdicts.title: Loss-scaler removal deleted ClippingStats.all_finite, the only signal that clipping silently zeroes non-finite per-example gradients; the sanitization it diagnosed is unchanged and nothing replaced the signal
verdicts.reasoning: Every mechanical link verified on the current tree. (1) dataclasses.fields(ClippingStats) == ['num_clipped','clipping_rate','batch_size'] (_clipped_fun.py:72-80); git show 7f55aae5 confirms _all_finite(), the aux_dict['all_finite'] production, the microbatch accumulation and the public field were all deleted in the same commit that removed _loss_scaler.py. (2) The sanitization is unchanged: torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) still heads clip_pytree (_pytree.py:600-607) and auto_scale (_pytree.py:464-471). (3) Reproduced the end-to-end symptom with the repo venv (torch 2.14): fp16 params, loss=((w*x)*s).sum(), x=[10,20,30,1000], s=[1,1,1,100] -> loss_values=[4.00e-3,8.00e-3,1.20e-2,40.0] all finite, grad_norms=tensor([10.,20.,30.,0.]), clipped_grad_norms=[0.9995,0.9995,0.9995,0.0000], and return_stats=True gives ClippingStats(num_clipped=3.0, clipping_rate=0.75, batch_size=4). Row 4's per-example gradient overflowed fp16 to inf, was zeroed, and nothing in either aux or stats reports it. (4) grep confirms no isfinite/isnan check anywhere in opaque-engine/dpsgd/transformers source other than the nan_to_num calls themselves, so there is indeed no replacement signal. WHERE THE FINDING OVERSTATES ITSELF, and why severity drops from medium to low: (a) the removal is explicitly documented as deliberate on the page that owns the knob - docs/user-guide/precision.md:47-48 'Opaque therefore does not expose a loss scaler or an aggregate pre-clipping finiteness signal' - so this is a documented design decision, not an incoherent removal; (b) the finding's load-bearing documentation claim ('grep -rn -iE non-finite|nonfinite|NaN/Inf|sanitiz docs/ -> no matches', therefore no user-facing document states the drop) is wrong: docs/reference/clipping.md:84 renders ::: opaque.dpsgd.clipping.fun with mkdocstrings, and clip_pytree (exported from that module, verified via __all__) carries 'NaN/Inf values: Replaced with zeros before clipping' in its Edge cases section, with auto_scale_pytree carrying 'NaN/Inf values are sanitized to zero before scaling'. Only the high-level clipped_grad docstring and docs/user-guide/clipping.md omit it; (c) the failure needs float16, which the library declares unsupported for training (precision.md:3-5 'Opaque does not provide dynamic loss scaling and DPTrainer does not support fp16 training'; bf16 - the recommended mode - has fp32 exponent range so per-example overflow to inf is as unlikely as in fp32); (d) no privacy consequence in either direction: a dropped record contributes nothing, which lowers realized sensitivity, and the adaptive-clipping quantile tracker being pushed downward by sanitized 0.0 norms only lowers the threshold and hence the accounted sensitivity. What remains after all that is a real but small observability/docs gap, actionable as one sentence in docs/user-guide/clipping.md plus optionally a read-only drop counter.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With low-level primitives under float16 (a mode DPTrainer rejects and the docs declare unsupported), a per-example gradient that overflows to inf is replaced by zeros inside clip_pytree/auto_scale, so that record contributes nothing to the released sum and no output says so. Reproduced: clipped_grad(..., clipping_norm=1.0, normalize_by=4, return_aux=True) on fp16 params with x=[10,20,30,1000], s=[1,1,1,100] returns loss_values all finite ([4.0e-3, 8.0e-3, 1.2e-2, 40.0]) but grad_norms=[10.,20.,30.,0.] and clipped_grad_norms=[0.9995,0.9995,0.9995,0.0]; the same call with return_stats=True returns ClippingStats(num_clipped=3.0, clipping_rate=0.75, batch_size=4) - no non-finite/drop field exists after 7f55aae5, and clipping_rate moves down (looks better) as records are dropped. Under adaptive_clipped_grad the quantile tracker sees the sanitized 0.0, so the threshold drifts down; that is utility loss, not privacy loss. No epsilon impact: dropping records only lowers realized sensitivity. The genuine gap is documentation and observability: precision.md states the aggregate finiteness signal is intentionally absent, and the zeroing is documented on clip_pytree / auto_scale_pytree (rendered into docs/reference/clipping.md via mkdocstrings), but neither clipped_grad's docstring nor docs/user-guide/clipping.md tells a user that records with non-finite per-example gradients are silently dropped and that grad_norms == 0.0 is the only ambiguous trace.

verdicts.title: Bounded-Gaussian removal's replacement docs advertise float16/bfloat16 as accepted compute_dtype values on the DPTrainer surface, contradicting precision.md's explicit "do not lower" rule for the same knob
verdicts.reasoning: All cited lines and measurements verified. docs/reference/transformers.md:196 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:138 both enumerate 'float16, bfloat16, float32, float64' for privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs.compute_dtype with no caveat; docs/user-guide/precision.md:68-70 carries the opposite guidance ('Do not lower precision without a separate numerical argument. Setting compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16 or torch.float16 can make the realized sensitivity and noise scale diverge from the accountant's model.'). _gaussian.py:59-61 defines _SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_DTYPES as all four and _validate_compute_dtype (111-124) accepts them with no warning path; _training_arguments.py:1637-1662 _normalize_gaussian_compute_dtype maps the string names with no warning; _dp_trainer.py:1676-1690 forwards the key verbatim into gaussian_noise; _gaussian.py:195-205 does center_c = center.to(compute_dtype) then sample = center_c + std*noise, i.e. the clipped sum is downcast before noise is added. I reproduced the numerics in the repo venv: over 200 trials with a fresh random 4096-dim unit-norm gradient on the clip sphere (C=1.0, noise_multiplier=1e-8) the worst realized ||released||_2 was 1.0001159 under compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16 vs 1.0000002 under float32 and 1.0000169 under float16 - i.e. ~1.2e-4 relative sensitivity excess for bf16, matching the finding's 1.23e-4. (Note the finding's harness detail matters: holding the gradient fixed across trials gives a max BELOW 1.0, because the center's rounding error is then identical every draw; the excess only appears with a fresh direction per trial.) Noise cardinality also reproduced: 2945 distinct values under bf16 vs 199721 under fp32 over 200000 draws at nm=1.0. SEVERITY DROPPED from medium to low, and the 'contradiction' framing is weaker than stated: a reference table enumerating the dtypes an API accepts is not a contradiction of a guidance page that warns against using two of them - the two pages have different jobs, and precision.md (the page the docs themselves designate as owning compute_dtype) already states exactly the hazard the finding describes. The measured effect is also tiny: 1.2e-4 relative sensitivity inflation measured, and even the adversarial bound is only ~2*2^-9 ~ 0.4% of C for bf16 (the clipped sum obeys ||S|| <= max_norm, so the rounding perturbation cannot scale beyond eps*max_norm), so the epsilon understatement is sub-percent. The coarse-discretization concern is real in principle (floating-point DP, Mironov 2012) but I did not convert it into an epsilon delta, and it too requires the deliberate opt-in. Actionable residue: repeat precision.md's caveat (or link it) in the two DPTrainer tables, and emit a one-time warning from _validate_compute_dtype when compute_dtype is narrower than float32.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A DPTrainer user who reads only docs/reference/transformers.md:196 or docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:138 sees 'float16, bfloat16, float32, float64' listed for privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['compute_dtype'] with no caveat and no pointer to docs/user-guide/precision.md:68-70, which is the page that tells them not to lower it. Setting {'compute_dtype': 'bfloat16'} is accepted silently by TrainingArguments (normalized to torch.bfloat16, no warning), forwarded verbatim into gaussian_noise, and _sample then downcasts the clipped sum (center.to(torch.bfloat16)) before adding noise. Measured over 200 draws of a fresh random 4096-dim gradient on the clip sphere with C=1.0 and noise_multiplier=1e-8: worst realized norm 1.0001159 under bfloat16 vs 1.0000002 under float32, i.e. a ~1.2e-4 relative excess over the C the accountant is calibrated to (adversarial bound ~0.4% of C for bf16); noise is also coarsely discretized (2945 distinct values vs 199721 over 200000 draws at nm=1.0), so the released mechanism is a discrete approximation of the continuous Gaussian the PLD assumes. Both effects require an explicit non-default opt-in that precision.md already warns against, and the epsilon understatement is sub-percent, so this is a docs cross-reference plus missing-warning gap rather than a silent privacy failure.

verdicts.title: Bounded-Gaussian removal left `bound` in the gaussian mechanism-kwargs allow-list, so the unknown-key error recommends the removed, privacy-unsound key
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced verbatim in the repo venv. _MECHANISM_KWARGS['gaussian'] is still frozenset({'bound','compute_dtype'}) (_training_arguments.py:229); _validate_privacy_kwargs (:273-289) prints sorted(allowed) in its unknown-key message; the explicit removal guard added by 873de427 sits at :1222-1228 in __post_init__ and runs before the allow-list check at :1353-1365. Executed: TrainingArguments(output_dir=..., privacy_noise_multiplier=1.0, clipping_norm=1.0, privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bnd': 3.0}) raises "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs contains unsupported keys for privacy_noise_mechanism='gaussian': ['bnd']. Allowed: ['bound', 'compute_dtype'].", and following that advice with {'bound': 3.0} raises "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound'] is unsupported: Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant." - so the first error's 'Allowed' list really does recommend a key the next validator refuses, and names a mechanism the library deliberately deleted. No upstream guard, config gate, or test rescues it. The secondary point also checks out: _dp_trainer.py:1678-1686 filters _gn_extra to _k == 'compute_dtype', so if the explicit guard at :1222 were ever refactored away, a surviving 'bound' key would be dropped silently instead of raised. Severity stays low: this is a misleading error message on a path that still fails closed; no epsilon impact, no silent wrong result today.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user mistypes a gaussian mechanism kwarg - TrainingArguments(..., privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bnd': 3.0}) - and gets "... unsupported keys for privacy_noise_mechanism='gaussian': ['bnd']. Allowed: ['bound', 'compute_dtype']." because _MECHANISM_KWARGS['gaussian'] at _training_arguments.py:229 still contains the removed 'bound' key. Following that advice with {'bound': 3.0} then raises "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound'] is unsupported: Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant." (the explicit guard at :1222-1228 runs first). Both messages reproduced verbatim. The configuration still fails closed in every case, so there is no epsilon or silent-corruption consequence; the defect is a self-contradicting error message plus a stale reference to the deleted bounded-Gaussian mechanism that would become load-bearing if the explicit guard were removed - at which point _dp_trainer.py's compute_dtype-only filter would drop 'bound' silently rather than reject it.

verdicts.title: Default-on fused-CE forward wrapper silently drops Cohere logit_scale / Granite logits_scaling / Gemma2 final_logit_softcapping on its non-fused branch
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced the numerical defect and verified every link. (1) Default-on gate: _factory.py:374-376 reads kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy') and falls back to `performance` when None; git show c0f95ced confirms the previous gate was kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy', False) plus a docstring saying it 'defaults to False'. _dp_trainer.py:844-850 always calls apply_model_patches(..., performance=True), and _dp_trainer.py:2437-2442 injects loss_only=True whenever _fused_forward_uses_marker (set at :866-875) is true. In my repro a bare apply_model_patches(m) installed the wrapper (loss_only appears in inspect.signature(m.forward).parameters) for Cohere, Granite, Gemma2 and Llama. (2) The fallback branch (cross_entropy.py:356-364) re-implements the HF tail as logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :]); loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs) with no family transform, while the fused branch threads logit_scale / logits_scaling / softcap into the kernels at :308-323. (3) The transform really lives in ForCausalLM.forward, not in loss_function: transformers 5.15.1 cohere/modeling_cohere.py:503 `logits = logits * self.logit_scale`, cohere2:481, granite/modeling_granite.py:497 `logits = logits / self.config.logits_scaling`, gemma2:527-530 softcapping tanh. Config defaults make this live: CohereConfig/Cohere2Config logit_scale=0.0625, Gemma2Config final_logit_softcapping=30.0 (GraniteConfig defaults logits_scaling=1.0, but real Granite checkpoints set it >1; Gemma3TextConfig defaults softcapping to None, so gemma3 is largely unaffected in practice). (4) Measured on CPU with tiny models, forcing the fallback by monkeypatching _fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported to False: fused branch matches the unpatched HF loss to 0.0000% for every family, while the fallback diverges for cohere (+0.27% at random init, +53.0% with lm_head scaled 10x, +602% at 50x) and granite (-0.36% / +10.0% / +215%); llama and gemma2-at-small-logits are unaffected. The divergence grows with logit magnitude, so on a real checkpoint it is large, not marginal. I also confirmed a device-independent silent route: passing a correctly padded shift_labels (shape [B,T]) on CPU yields patched=6.37459 vs HF=4.16521 (+53.0%) with no error; passing shift_labels of shape [B,T-1] or logits_to_keep!=0 instead raises a ValueError from fixed_cross_entropy rather than corrupting. (5) No test covers the fallback: test_fused_ce_text_family_parity.py only parametrizes olmo2/olmo3/smollm3/ministral/glm4 (none of the scaled families), its scaling tests assert the fused path only ('fallback should not run'), and test_fused_ce_wrapper_preserves_logits_to_keep passes labels=None so the wrapper delegates to original() at :204-220. REACHABILITY, which is where I lower critical to high: the CUDA route is a plain boolean I could not execute (no GPU here) but is trivially readable - use_fused_ce requires (hidden_states.is_cuda and dtype in (bf16, fp16)) or not is_cuda, so CUDA + fp32 hidden states takes the fallback, and DPTrainer defaults bf16=False (_training_arguments.py:415) with _setup_precision leaving _train_dtype at whatever the caller pre-placed (_dp_trainer.py:904-905, no forcing, no warning). That combination needs fp32 model weights on CUDA: it is a documented first-class mode (docs/user-guide/precision.md '## float32 training') and an offered example flag (examples/train_dpftrl.py --dtype float32), but it is NOT what the most literal default flow produces, because transformers 5.15 from_pretrained defaults dtype='auto' (modeling_utils.py:3986, :4136-4137) and cohere/granite/gemma2 checkpoints are bf16, which routes to the correct fused branch. On CPU/MPS the fused (chunked) branch always wins, so those hosts are safe unless a caller supplies shift_labels. Impact is utility, not privacy: clipping and noise still apply to whatever gradient is produced, so epsilon is unaffected.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: DPTrainer DP-SFT of a Cohere / Cohere2 / Granite / Gemma2 checkpoint loaded in float32 on a CUDA GPU with the default bf16=False. apply_model_patches(..., performance=True) installs the fused-CE forward wrapper by default since c0f95ced (#988), the trainer sets loss_only=True, but use_fused_ce (cross_entropy.py:282-292) requires half-precision hidden states on CUDA, so fp32 hidden states fall into the else branch at :356-364, which recomputes logits = lm_head(hidden) and calls self.loss_function without the family's post-lm_head transform (Cohere logits*0.0625, Granite logits/logits_scaling, Gemma2 softcapping tanh). Every per-example loss and gradient is then computed on the wrong objective, with no exception and no warning; DP clipping and noise still apply, so the run looks healthy and epsilon is unaffected. Measured on CPU with tiny models by forcing the same branch: the fused branch matches unpatched HF exactly (0.0000%), while the fallback gives cohere +0.27% at random init, +53.0% with lm_head scaled 10x and +602% at 50x, and granite -0.36% / +10.0% / +215% - the error grows with logit magnitude, so a trained checkpoint is badly wrong, not marginally. A device-independent silent route also exists: a caller (e.g. a padding-free collator) passing shift_labels of shape [B,T] reproduces cohere +53.0% on CPU. Not reachable on CPU/MPS otherwise, and not reachable with the transformers-5 default dtype='auto' (bf16 checkpoints route to the correct fused branch), so the trigger is fp32-on-CUDA - a documented supported mode (docs/user-guide/precision.md 'float32 training', examples/train_dpftrl.py --dtype float32) rather than the most literal default. No test pins the fallback branch for any scaled family.
